title: Customer Ageing
blurb: What each customer really owes JIVO after netting off cash already banked and credit notes already raised that SAP never matched to the invoice — and how much of the 'debtors' figure is JIVO's own branch, intercompany and staff accounts rather than anyone external.
grain: One SUMMARY row = one KIND of customer account (BRANCH / INTERCO / STAFF / TRADE) for one company, plus a fifth GROUPING SETS roll-up row literal 'ZZ_TOTAL'; 5 rows per book, 15 in all. One DETAIL row = one customer card (OCRD CardType='C') that has any of an open invoice, a non-zero balance, an unapplied receipt or an open credit note, with the seven ageing buckets as COLUMNS, not as rows; 642 Oil / 100 Mart / 451 Bev at 2026-08-22T19:05 IST.
faceted_total_row: column KIND, value 'ZZ_TOTAL'. Summing a money column across all five rows returns exactly 2x. TRADE is KIND=='TRADE'; the non-trade block is KIND in ('BRANCH','INTERCO','STAFF').

charts.title: From SAP's number to the real one
charts.why: The correction, drawn. RAW_OPEN_INR (ZZ_TOTAL) → less UNAPPLIED_CREDIT_INR → book EFF_OPEN_INR → less BRANCH → less INTERCO → less STAFF → the TRADE receivable. On Oil that is ₹182.17 Cr → ₹110.52 Cr → ₹7.35 Cr in six labelled steps, and each step is a link to its own derivation. Every consumer who gets this section wrong got it wrong at one of these six bars.

charts.title: Ageing profile by account kind
charts.why: Four bars side by side make the classification argument without a sentence: Oil's BRANCH bar is 78% in the 365-day segment (₹60.18 Cr of frozen inter-registration GST transfers) while TRADE is front-loaded. Uses --age-nd + --age1..--age6 with a value label on every segment, because the two lightest ramp steps fail 3:1 on cream.

charts.title: How few customers are the whole book
charts.why: Bars plus a cumulative line over TRADE detail rows. 6 cards reach 80% of Oil's book; ONE card reaches 80% of Mart's (R K WORLDINFOCOM, 88.2%) and of Bev's (BLESSING ADVERTISING, 82.4%). It tells a collector that two of the three books are a single phone call, which no table conveys at a glance.

charts.title: Age against size — what to chase first
charts.why: One dot per TRADE customer, x = days since the oldest item still carrying money, y = amount, each dot a link to party.html. Big-and-old separates instantly from big-and-current: Oil's FUTURE RETAIL (₹94.5 L at 2,445 days, company in insolvency) sits alone in the top-right, while WAL MART's ₹98.9 L sits at 254 days and is not a problem. A sorted table cannot show two dimensions at once.

charts.title: The collection list — overdue more than 60 days
charts.why: Top 12 TRADE cards by ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS, which is the file's own sort order, each linked to party.html. This is the panel an operator prints. Carries the lower-bound caveat inline because the ranking is FIFO-dependent.

charts.title: Where the unmatched cash is sitting
charts.why: ₹66.2 Cr of Oil and ₹89.8 Cr of Mart TRADE receipts are banked and never knocked off an invoice — the operational CAUSE of the whole correction, and a backlog somebody can actually clear. A treemap answers 'which accounts do I clear first' in one glance; the equivalent table is 453 Oil rows long. Clamp the one −0.01 rupee cell to zero for area, and say so.

charts.title: Whose money is in 'debtors'
charts.why: TRADE / BRANCH / INTERCO / STAFF as a share of the book, ZZ_TOTAL excluded. Oil is 93.4% JIVO's own money, Mart 38.9%, Bev 20.1%. Four slices, fixed --c1..--c4 order, value labels — it is the single fastest way to stop someone quoting the ₹110 Cr.

charts.title: How much of SAP's open A/R is real
charts.why: EFF_OPEN_INR as a fraction of RAW_OPEN_INR on the TRADE row: Oil 9.7%, Mart 9.0%, Bev 76.9%. One number per book that says how far you can trust a raw SAP A/R report, and it makes Beverages' different character (a book that is mostly real and mostly one late customer) visible against the other two.

traps: ZZ_TOTAL is a FIFTH ROW in the same array as BRANCH/INTERCO/STAFF/TRADE (GROUPING SETS, column KIND, literal value 'ZZ_TOTAL'). Summing any money column across all rows returns exactly 2x the truth. The TOTAL row is KIND=='ZZ_TOTAL'; every other consumer must filter by KIND. This is the section's live landmine and v1's renderer only just avoids it.

DocStatus='O' is not solvency at JIVO (C-0019). Raw open vs credit-adjusted on the TRADE book: Oil ₹75.86 Cr → ₹7.35 Cr (10.3x), Mart ₹113.84 Cr → ₹10.30 Cr (11.1x), Bev ₹5.00 Cr → ₹3.84 Cr (1.3x). Anything that reads RAW_OPEN_INR and calls it a receivable is wrong by an order of magnitude on two of the three books.

N_CUSTOMERS and N_OPEN_INV are SAP's UNCORRECTED counts. Pairing them with EFF_OPEN_INR re-commits the very error the section corrects: ₹7.35 Cr ÷ 11,499 invoices = ₹6,396 each, against the truth of ₹55,509 across 1,325. Use N_EFF_CUSTOMERS and N_EFF_INV; show the SAP count struck through if at all.

The bucket split is an ASSUMPTION, the total is a measurement. EFF_OPEN_INR is identical to the paisa whether credit is consumed oldest-first or newest-first; the BUCKETS are not. Mart's 60-day-plus figure moves from ₹30.14 L (shipped, FIFO) to ₹8.46 Cr (newest-first) — 28x. Oil 1.18x, Bev 1.01x. Every overdue figure on this page is a LOWER BOUND and must say so, Mart loudest.

Never subtract UNAPPLIED_RECEIPTS_INR or OPEN_CREDIT_NOTES_INR from the receivable. They are already inside OCRD.Balance, which is what EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at. Subtracting Oil's ₹66.2 Cr of unapplied receipts from its ₹7.35 Cr trade book would produce a large negative receivable out of correct data.

EFF_OPEN_INR is capped at the ledger debit, so BAL_NOT_IN_INV_INR of trade debit is carried by no open invoice and is never aged: Oil ₹65.07 L (8.13% of the trade ledger debit), Mart ₹13.09 L (1.26%), Bev ₹45,378 (0.12%). The headline is a disclosed understatement of the debit book. Show OCRD_DEBIT_INR beside it, never instead of it.

OCRD_CREDIT_INR is stored NEGATIVE (JIVO sign convention: −ve = JIVO owes the party). Adding it to OCRD_DEBIT_INR silently nets customers in advance against customers in arrears and produces a 'net receivable' that means nothing. The detail twin CUSTOMER_ADVANCE stores the same money POSITIVE — mixing the two flips a sign.

MIGRATED_OPEN_INR: Oil's 365-day-plus TRADE bucket is 96.6% migrated pre-SAP openings (invoices dated exactly at go-live 2024-09-30, carrying true original due dates back to 2017). Calling it 'debt that rotted since go-live' is wrong. The 0.00 in Mart and Bev is a TRUE zero — their first invoices are 2024-10-03 and 2024-10-04 and neither book has an opening batch — but the date is HARD-CODED and Oil-specific, so a fourth company book would need its own go-live checked.

OLDEST_OPEN_DUE / OLDEST_DUE is the oldest date that still carries money AFTER credit application, not the oldest open document. It jumps forward when a receipt is matched, and it deliberately means something different here than in vendor-ageing.sql, which reports the raw oldest bill. Do not compare the two sections' oldest dates.

The detail row count is NOT N_CUSTOMERS and must never be asserted equal. The detail keeps cards that exist only as an unapplied receipt or an open credit note (642 Oil rows vs 379 counted), and 25 Oil / 3 Mart / 9 Bev cards carry sub-paise dust balances that are <>0 in SQL but round to 0.00 at 2 dp. N_EFF_CUSTOMERS for Oil TRADE is 89 while detail rows with ADJ_OPEN>0 number 85 — same dust. Assert the money, never the headcount.

Classification divergences that are real and deliberately unfixed: Oil CUSTA000242 AKAL INFORMATION SYSTEMS LTD (group DEBTORS, ₹10,000) reads TRADE here and INTERCO in both vendor-ageing.sql and open-item-list.sql — verified live 2026-08-22, the one ACCT_KIND mismatch across 229 shared Oil cards. And 8-9 employee imprest cards filed in a STATE group instead of 'STAFF CUSTOMER' read TRADE (Oil ₹3,555 · Mart ₹1,957 · Bev ₹11,562 incl. CUSTA000902 NAVNEET SINGH, which has no 'IMPREST' in its name). Fixing either in one file without the other breaks the summary↔detail tie.

CUSTA000356 'FREE SAMPLE' is classified TRADE in all three books and carries a real ageing (Oil ₹91,239 with ₹85,509 over 60 days; Bev ₹57,809). Nothing in OCRG or the card name marks it internal. It is almost certainly not collectable and it has never been checked with Accounts — do not put it on a collection list without a footnote.

UNAPPLIED_RCPT can be NEGATIVE by a rounding paisa (Oil CUSTA000482 METRO CASH & CARRY = −0.01). Any treemap, log scale or sqrt-area chart over that column must clamp, and a 'top unmatched receipts' sort must not assume the column is non-negative.

Cross-section: open-item-list's CARD_OPEN_GROSS is NOT this section's RAW_OPEN — it folds unapplied receipts into 'gross open'. Oil CUSTA000844 ILAHI CO. reads ₹44.71 L there and ₹24.71 L here, a ₹20 L AR receipt. Its CARD_BALANCE, however, IS the same OCRD.Balance and matched on 229/21/220 shared cards with zero mismatches — that column is a valid cross-file check, CARD_OPEN_GROSS is not.

A back-dated {{ASOF}} is not a point-in-time A/R. OCRD.Balance and PaidToDate are the CURRENT snapshot — SAP keeps no per-date history — so a past as-of ages today's open items against an older calendar. Measured on Oil: --as-of 2026-03-31 gives ₹80.34 Cr adjusted against ₹108.86 Cr today, and ₹2.87 Cr of trade against ₹7.43 Cr. The cut-off is on DocDate only, so an invoice cancelled yesterday vanishes from a last-month run.

Group totals are NOT intercompany-eliminated. Oil, Mart and Bev trade with each other and each book carries the other as a customer; adding the three EFF_OPEN_INR figures double-counts JIVO's own money. Per-company is the only figure that means anything, and the INTERCO row names the amount in each book.

A KIND row with NOTDUE_INR = 0 and EFF_OPEN_INR > 0 is REAL, not a missing bucket: Oil BRANCH, Mart BRANCH/INTERCO/STAFF and Bev BRANCH/INTERCO are 100% overdue. Rendering that as an empty bar or 'no data' misreports a book that is entirely past due.

Every CO_* column in the detail (CO_RAW_OPEN … CO_ADJ_OVERDUE_60PLUS_TRADE) is a company-level total repeated on EVERY row by SUM() OVER (). Read one row. Summing the column multiplies it by 642 / 100 / 451.

data.json is being rewritten under readers roughly every 2 minutes by the VPS refresh loop. A consumer that reads the file twice in one pass can mix two builds — I hit exactly this and briefly saw ZZ_TOTAL disagree with the sum of its KIND rows by ₹40.32 L. Load once into memory, and stamp every derived figure with the generated_at it came from.
empty_states: summary array is empty: HANA's GROUPING SETS ((KIND),()) emits NO grand-total row over empty input, so an empty book is zero rows — not a ZZ_TOTAL row of zeros. Render empty('No customer accounts in this book') and never synthesise a total.

A KIND row is absent entirely (a book with no STAFF or no INTERCO cards): render 'no <kind> accounts in this book', not a ₹0 card. Verified today all four KINDs exist in all three books, so an absent KIND means the classification changed and deserves to be noticed.

ZZ_TOTAL row missing while KIND rows are present: do NOT silently sum the KIND rows into a headline. Render empty('roll-up row missing — totals not computed') and flag the section, because the roll-up is absent only when the GROUPING SETS shape changed.

detail array empty while summary has rows: the per-customer panel, the pareto, the scatter and the treemap all render empty('per-customer detail did not build') with the section error text. Never fall back to plotting the four KIND rows as if they were customers.

MIGRATED_OPEN_INR == 0 for Mart and Bev: a TRUE zero (verified — neither book has an opening batch), so it renders as 'none — this book has no pre-SAP opening batch', which is different from a null. If the COLUMN is missing, render 'not computed'.
OLDEST_OPEN_DUE / OLDEST_DUE is NULL (537 Oil / 70 Mart / 253 Bev detail rows, and any KIND whose EFF_OPEN is 0): render 'nothing outstanding' — never a date, never 0 days, never today's date.

EFF_OPEN_INR is 0 but RAW_OPEN_INR is large (a card fully covered by unapplied credit — 541 of 642 Oil detail rows): show ₹0 outstanding WITH the raw figure and the credit beside it. A bare zero here reads as 'no invoices', which is the opposite of the truth.

OD60P_INR == 0 with EFF_OPEN_INR > 0 (Mart INTERCO and STAFF today): a real, healthy zero — label it 'nothing over 60 days', and keep the FIFO lower-bound caveat visible because a different allocation could make it non-zero.

sections['customer-ageing']['errors'] is non-empty for a company: the whole section renders as failed for that company with the error text and the last-good generated_at. Never partially render from a stale slice without saying it is stale.

A KPI's source column is absent from the row (a schema change or a rolled-back SQL edit): render 'not computed — column <NAME> missing from this build', never 0. v1 already guards N_EFF_INV this way with a == null fallback; keep that pattern.
